findings.title: Scope, boundaries, dependency direction, and NFR restate align with plan 140 and architecture 140
findings.description: The slice implements exactly the two interventions in plan entry 149 and nothing more; distance-ranked k-nearest and GPU prefix sum are explicitly deferred, matching the plan's "Out of scope for 149" list. It preserves the `quadrants-fused` setup/tick API so slice 146 stays unblocked (correct dependency direction: 149 → 145 implementation, 149 → 146 interface stability), declares no changes to `TickResult`, the world server, or the numpy/numba backends, and keeps the fused kernel outside `SpatialQuery`/`BulkForce` as the architecture's GPU-fused-tick principle requires. The parent architecture NFR is restated with a specific target at line 116 ("Tier 2 target is 60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA") and the slice gate (A3 ≥ 100 TPS) is justified as headroom above it. Config validation of `S` is a hard error at config-load time with no silent clamp, consistent with the project's "never use silent fallback values" rule.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough invokes a bench harness and CLI flags that do not exist
findings.description: Steps 2–5 all drive `python scripts/bench.py --backend … --config … --N … --ticks … --subdivision-factor … --parity-check …`. There is no `scripts/bench.py` (scripts/ contains only the two slice-148 measurement scripts), and the real harness entry point (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py`, `python -m migratory.bench.cli` / `python -m migratory.bench`) accepts only `--workload`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir`, and the `--list-*` flags — no `--config`, `--N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor`, or `--parity-check`. Slices 145 and 148 verified through `uv run python -m migratory.bench.cli --backend … --workload …`, with tick counts coming from the workload YAML. As written, the gate procedure for A2/A3 cannot be executed; the requirement it leaves unmet is a reproducible gate-measurement procedure. Either name the real CLI and where `S` is supplied, or explicitly scope adding a flag/script as slice work.

findings.title: Gate workload `mid-flock-50k` currently runs N=100k, not the N=50k the success criteria reference
findings.description: A2/A3 and the default gate config ("`mid-flock-50k` workload, `S=3`, `max_neighbors=32`") are all stated at N=50k, and the problem statement's ~5000-agents/cell occupancy is the N=50k two-flock measurement from slice 148. The checked-in `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml` has `n: 100000` and `world_size: [1536.0, 1536.0]` (its own description text still claims an N scaled from mid-flock), so running the named workload produces N=100k numbers at a density that does not reproduce the ~5000/cell operating point. The design should state whether the workload is corrected to N=50k, a new N=50k workload is added, or the criteria are re-anchored to whatever `mid-flock-50k` actually runs — otherwise A2/A3 cannot be demonstrated at the N they name.

findings.title: A5's primary verification mechanism is documented as unavailable on the gate host
findings.description: A5 offers "`nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log", and Step 4 suggests `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` "or equivalent". Slice 148's envelope measurement (148-notes.envelope-measurement.md, §2A) recorded that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump`, and `nvcc` are not installed on the CUDA host and that the working method was inspecting cached PTX for `.local` declarations (baseline: 0, confirming no spill). That note also shows the kernel profiler did not yield the needed register/local-memory figures. A5 should name the method that actually worked on this host (PTX cache inspection for `.local`) rather than a toolchain known to be absent.

findings.title: The configuration carrier for `S` is unspecified; "BenchConfig" does not exist
findings.description: The component diagram sources `cell_size` and `S` from a `BenchConfig` object, but the harness has no such type — configuration arrives as `Workload` YAML (`src/migratory/bench/workload.py`, whose loader raises on missing fields) plus CLI arguments, and `GpuAgentState.setup()` derives `cell_size` from `max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` (quadrants_fused_state.py:150-152). The design says "the bench harness passes `cell_size` at setup; it reads from config" without naming where `S` lives: workload YAML schema, CLI flag, or backend parameter. This leaves two requirements unmet: (1) a single named carrier for `S`, and (2) one centralized home for the `S=1` default (project convention forbids scattered magic defaults). Related minor inaccuracy: line 80 attributes `grid_w`/`grid_h` computation to `build_spatial_hash`; that computation is in `GpuAgentState.setup()`.

findings.title: Plan entry's 7-neighbor benchmark target is absent from the design
findings.description: Plan 140 entry 149 carries a biological note making "the 7-neighbor operating point … a benchmark target" for this slice, and the slice 148 re-diagnosis (which the plan entry mirrors) calls it "a meaningful operating point to benchmark", noting the early-exit gain scales with `candidates_scanned / max_neighbors` and is even larger at k=7. The design contains no criterion, workload, or verification run at `max_neighbors=7` — all gates are fixed at `max_neighbors=32`. Either add a 7-neighbor measurement pass or explicitly defer it with a named owner; as written, scope the plan entry assigns to this slice is silently dropped.

findings.title: Candidate-count arithmetic in the Intervention 2 interaction analysis is internally inconsistent
findings.description: "With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000. With both: candidates loaded ~555, exits after ~32." The slice's own source (148-notes.rediagnosis.md, Intervention 2) computes the S=3 scan as 49 cells × ~555 ≈ 27,000 candidates scanned, with early exit then limiting acceptances to ~32; line 56 of this same document correctly derives ~555 as per-cell occupancy. "~5000" and "~555" conflate per-cell occupancy with total candidates scanned. The gates are empirical so this doesn't block implementation, but an implementer sanity-checking scan counts against the design would misread a correct result as a broken subdivision; correct the arithmetic to the re-diagnosis figures.

findings.title: "CPU fallback" for Mac verification does not exist for this backend
findings.description: "A1 and A4 can be verified on Mac (Metal or CPU fallback)." `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner._select_arch()` raises on any platform other than Linux/CUDA or Darwin/Metal — there is no CPU fallback for the fused backend (slice 145 design: "there is no CPU fallback"). Mac verification means Metal only; the numpy backend serves as the parity reference, not as a fallback runner for this backend.
